_note: Every region the forecast can cover. Each one is a separate daily run and
its own folder under docs/data/, so the page can switch between them.
COVERAGE IS NOT UNIFORM, and the app says so per region:
species_file  a validated species pack, or null. The pack in this repo
is Adriatic and its legal rules are Croatian - applying it
to Greece or Spain would be confidently wrong, so those
regions run structure + conditions only until someone
builds a pack for them.
jurisdiction  whose fishing law applies. Closed seasons and minimum
sizes in species.json are Croatian ONLY.
enabled       whether the daily workflow computes it. Each enabled
region costs a few hundred KB of output and about 5
seconds of compute, so turn on what you use.
Bathymetry is EMODnet, which covers European seas only. Outside that
footprint the relief term has nothing to work with and the region should
not be added at all.

WORLDWIDE: regions outside EMODnet's footprint fall back to NOAA's global SRTM15+ at 15 arc-seconds (~300-450 m). The relief term cannot see a reef at that scale, and the app says so per region rather than pretending.

WHY ENABLING A REGION CHANGES THE SPECIES LIST: point mode covers conditions and structure anywhere on Earth, but the species it names come from regionContaining() in docs/index.html, which only sees regions that ACTUALLY RAN - that is, enabled ones. Outside every enabled region the app falls back to the coarse ocean-basin classifier in BIOME_RULES, which is a reference list for that stretch of ocean rather than a pack tuned to the coast, and which deliberately carries no legal sizes or seasons at all. So enabling the region you actually dive is the single thing that most improves what the app tells you about fish there.

Enabling also brings the extras a region alone provides: exclusion zones, charted wrecks, depth contours, precomputed per-species maps, GPX export, Sentinel-2 turbidity and the Copernicus temperature profile. Each costs roughly 600 KB of output and a few seconds of compute per day.
Enabled now: novigrad, cascais, faro-ria-formosa. The rest are defined and ready - flip enabled to true on any of them.

regions.name: Novigrad, Istria
regions.note: The home region. Species pack, closed seasons and exclusion zones all checked here; everything else in this file inherits or omits them.

regions.name: Cascais, Estoril and Parede
regions.note: Guincho round Cabo Raso to Oeiras, including the Parede and Sao Pedro reefs. Atlantic, not Mediterranean: real swell, real tides and colder water than the species depth bands were tuned for, so read the temperature fits as indicative. The Atlanto-Mediterranean pack does apply here - sargus, vulgaris, aurata, labrax, dentex, umbra, octopus and sepia all have genuine Atlantic Iberian ranges - and legal/PT.json carries the EU floor sizes for exactly that list. Closed seasons for PT are NOT researched. The Avencas marine protected area sits inside this box and is NOT masked: no exclusions file exists for it. Check it yourself before you get in.

regions.name: Faro and the Ria Formosa
regions.note: The barrier islands off Faro and Olhao. This is the region that exposed the land-mask problem: the Ria Formosa spits are 200-600 m wide, narrower than a global bathymetry cell, so the depth grid averaged them out to open water and the score wash and depth lines were drawn straight across the beach and the lagoon. The OSM coastline mask exists because of this coast. Note that the whole lagoon system is a Parque Natural with its own rules, and none of them are encoded here.

regions.name: Sagres and Cabo Sao Vicente
regions.note: The south-west corner, where the west and south coasts meet. The shelter term earns its keep here: one side is always in the lee. Inside the Costa Vicentina natural park, which is not masked.

regions.name: Peniche and the Berlengas
regions.note: The Berlengas are a nature reserve with a no-take core that is NOT masked here. Exposed Atlantic swell; the workability floor will rule most days out, which is realistic.

regions.name: Madeira, south coast
regions.note: Macaronesian, so the Azores pack fits far better than the mainland one - amberjack and barracuda country rather than the Diplodus/Sparus mix. Volcanic and very steep: the depth gate does most of the work because the 25 m band is often only a few hundred metres wide.

regions.name: Rias Baixas, Galicia
regions.note: Cold, green, Atlantic and heavily fished. The rias are drowned river valleys, so the water mask and the coastline mask both matter more here than almost anywhere else. Galicia has its own regional rules that are NOT encoded.

regions.name: Costa Blanca and Tabarca
regions.note: Tabarca is Spain's oldest marine reserve and spearfishing is banned there outright. It is NOT masked. Warm, clear and much calmer than the Atlantic regions.

regions.name: Mallorca, north coast
regions.note: The Serra de Tramuntana coast. Steep-to and clear, with several reserves along it that are not masked. The visibility model was tuned on a turbid shelf and will read low here.

regions.name: Sicily, west and the Egadi
regions.note: The Egadi islands are the largest marine protected area in the Mediterranean and are zoned, not uniformly open. None of that zoning is encoded here. Italian rules apply; closed seasons for IT are not researched.

regions.name: Crete, north coast
regions.note: Meltemi country like the Cyclades, so shelter dominates. Very clear water; the visibility model understates it badly. Greek closed seasons are not researched.

regions.name: Kvarner — Krk and Cres
regions.note: Same jurisdiction and broadly the same species as Novigrad, but deeper and rockier. NO exclusion zones are defined here yet - check protected areas yourself.

regions.name: Split and Brač channel
regions.note: Croatian rules apply, so the closed seasons hold. Clearer and deeper than Istria; the species depth bands were tuned on a shallow shelf and will read low here.

regions.name: Piran and the Gulf
regions.note: Structure and conditions only. Slovenian fishing law differs from Croatian, so the species pack is deliberately NOT applied - showing Croatian closed seasons here would be worse than showing nothing. Mediterranean species pack applies; sizes are the EU floor and closed seasons for this country are NOT researched.

regions.name: Gulf of Trieste
regions.note: Italian rules. Needs its own species pack before the target view means anything. Mediterranean species pack applies; sizes are the EU floor and closed seasons for this country are NOT researched.

regions.name: Costa Brava
regions.note: Different species assemblage and Spanish regional rules. Mediterranean species pack applies; sizes are the EU floor and closed seasons for this country are NOT researched.

regions.name: Sardinia, north-west
regions.note: Deep and clear. The visibility model was tuned on a turbid shelf and will understate clarity badly here. Mediterranean species pack applies; sizes are the EU floor and closed seasons for this country are NOT researched.

regions.name: Corsica, west coast
regions.note: French rules, several marine reserves. Do not dive this on the app alone. Mediterranean species pack applies; sizes are the EU floor and closed seasons for this country are NOT researched.

regions.name: Algarve, central
regions.note: Atlantic, not Mediterranean, but the same species pack applies: sargus, vulgaris, aurata, labrax, dentex, umbra, octopus and sepia are all Atlanto-Mediterranean species with real Atlantic Iberian ranges, and legal/PT.json already carries size and season entries for exactly this list. Depth and season fields are still Adriatic-tuned and colder, tidal Atlantic water will read them low - real tides and real swell here too.

regions.name: Paros and Naxos
regions.note: Meltemi dominates everything here; the shelter term should do more work than usual. Mediterranean species pack applies; sizes are the EU floor and closed seasons for this country are NOT researched.

regions.name: Faial and Pico channel
regions.note: Mid-Atlantic volcanic. EMODnet reaches here so the structure map is at full resolution. Own species pack (species_azores.json) - amberjack, blacktail comber and barracuda country rather than the Mediterranean's Diplodus/Sparus mix. Note: spearfishing for dusky grouper is banned regionally in the Azores even though it is present here; it is deliberately left off the species list.

regions.name: Tenerife, south-west
regions.note: EMODnet coverage, so full-resolution structure. legal/ES.json already carries size and season entries for the same 8-species pack used elsewhere, and sargus, vulgaris, dentex, umbra, octopus and sepia are all well documented in Canarian waters; aurata and labrax range here too but are less dominant than on the mainland. Two genuinely common local targets - vieja (Sparisoma cretense) and mero (Epinephelus marginatus) - are not in this pack yet.

regions.name: Oahu, west shore
regions.note: Global bathymetry tier only. Hawaii has excellent NOAA CUDEM coverage at 3-10 m that this does not yet use - that would be the single biggest upgrade here. Own species pack (species_oahu.json): uhu, kumu, omilu, ulua, roi and mu.

regions.name: Palos Verdes and Catalina
regions.note: Kelp forest diving. California has its own licence and species rules that are NOT encoded. Own species pack (species_socal.json): sheephead, kelp bass, halibut, lingcod, white seabass, yellowtail.

regions.name: Florida Keys, upper
regions.note: Reef. Large protected areas where spearfishing is banned outright and none of them are encoded here. Own species pack (species_florida_keys.json): hogfish, mutton/yellowtail/mangrove snapper, black/gag grouper.

regions.name: False Bay
regions.note: Cold, surgy, and shark country. The model knows nothing about any of that. Own species pack (species_capetown.json): galjoen, red roman, hottentot, yellowtail.

regions.name: Rottnest and Perth
regions.note: AusSeabed publishes much finer bathymetry than the global tier used here. Own species pack (species_rottnest.json): dhufish, pink snapper, samson fish, baldchin groper, breaksea cod. Rottnest's own sanctuary zones are NOT masked.

regions.name: Northland, Poor Knights
regions.note: The Poor Knights themselves are a no-take marine reserve. This region covers the wider coast; the reserve is NOT masked. Own species pack (species_poorknights.json): kingfish, snapper, trevally, John Dory - describes the fishable coast, not the reserve.

regions.name: Bali, north coast
regions.note: Indo-Pacific reef. Own species pack (species_bali.json): coral trout, red bass, GT, green jobfish, barracuda. Parrotfish deliberately left off - many local communities avoid spearing them for reef health.

regions.name: Okinawa, west coast
regions.note: Subtropical reef. Japanese prefectural rules on spearfishing are strict and vary; none are encoded. Own species pack (species_okinawa.json): irabucha, mibai, akajin, taman, snapper. Humphead wrasse deliberately left off - it is IUCN Endangered.
